html:
Vienna is the capital of Austria, on the Danube where the Alps meet the plains of central Europe. For six centuries it was the home of the Habsburgs and one of the great capitals of Europe.

It began as Vindobona, a Roman army camp on the Danube frontier. The Habsburgs took it in the 1270s and ruled from it until 1918, and for most of that time they were also emperors of the Holy Roman Empire. As Christendom's bulwark against the Ottomans, it survived the siege of 1529 and a second siege in 1683, whose failure began the Ottoman retreat from Hungary.

In the 1700s and 1800s it became the capital of music. Mozart and Beethoven worked there, as did Haydn and Schubert. After Napoleon's fall the Congress of Vienna of 1814 and 1815 redrew the map of Europe. The city rose in the revolutions of 1848.

As the capital of the Austrian Empire and then Austria-Hungary, it grew to about two million people by 1910, drawing migrants from every part of the empire. Around 1900 it was a hothouse of new ideas, from Sigmund Freud's psychoanalysis to modern art and architecture. After 1918 it was the oversized capital of a small republic. Germany annexed Austria in 1938, and the city was occupied by the four Allied powers until 1955. It now hosts United Nations agencies.
sum: Vienna is the capital of Austria, on the Danube where the Alps meet the plains of central Europe. For six centuries it was the home of the Habsburgs and one of the great capitals of Europe.
